From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Order form change window & legal waterfall — change order proposal for Cirrus Health

Mira — thanks again for the sync this morning. Per our conversation attached is a draft change order (CO_Cirrus_20261119_draft.docx) that: 1) adds 100K throughput units (sku: THR-100K) to the existing order form, 2) introduces a blended monthly rate for the add-on (see pricing table on p.2), and 3) proposes a phased billing start (net 30 from signature, with a 30-day retro window if prod cutover happens earlier).

High level asks:
- Please confirm whether your procurement team can accept the phased billing start and the retroactive credit approach.
- Legal: there are two MSA cross-references (Exhibit B and Exhibit F) — we left them explicit but welcome any redline.
- Ops: we estimate a 3-week implementation to assemble the additional capacity behind the dedicated pool. Laura — can you confirm ops ETA and whether we should include an explicit fallback SKU if we can’t provision the THR-100K on time?

If this looks directionally right, can Cirrus legal provide redlines by EOD Monday (11/22) so we can finalize for signature? We can push an updated PDF for DocuSign as soon as we have agreement.

Attachments: CO_Cirrus_20261119_draft.docx (redline-ready), pricing-exhibit-draft.xlsx (referenced inline)

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien

connor@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

Subject: Re: Order form change window & legal waterfall — change order proposal for Cirrus Health

Connor — thanks for sending. High level: we like the phased approach but have a couple of legal and security asks before committing. Looping our in-house counsel (legal@cirrushealth.com).

Preliminary items from Cirrus:
- Please remove or clarify the "rollback protection" language on p.3. We prefer a defined rollback process tied to performance KPIs rather than an open-ended clause.
- Data handling: our security team needs confirmation that the additional throughput will be served in the same VPC/tenant and that logs/audit trails are retained for 12 months. Can you confirm?
- SOC 2 evidence: our procurement requires current SOC 2 Type II report; please attach or share a link to the secure evidence room.

We will aim to get top-line redlines back by Monday but legal may itemize a few alternative wording suggestions.

— Mira
Mira Patel
Procurement Manager, Cirrus Health

Irene — can you propose replacement wording for the rollback protection clause that ties rollback to two measurable KPIs (successful warm-up, latency SLAs) and gives a 14-day cure period? Also please confirm whether referencing Exhibit F (implementation runbook) is sufficient for operational fallback obligations. Attachment: ChangeOrder_v2_redline.docx (I’ve incorporated one set of clean edits).

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Mira Patel <mira@cirrushealth.com>, Cirrus Health Legal <legal@cirrushealth.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 12:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FW: Order form change window & legal waterfall — Cirrus change order (legal suggested language)

Connor — thanks for the context. I reviewed the draft and drafted alternative language that tightens the rollback protection and ties obligations to Exhibit F. Key points below (I've attached a marked-up file CO_Cirrus_legal_markups.docx):

Proposed clause (suggested replacement for section 3.2, "Rollback Protection"):
"If, within 45 days of the effective date of this Change Order, Customer demonstrates that the new capacity materially degrades Service availability or latency by more than 15% against the baseline defined in Exhibit F, Customer may request remediation. Redwood will have 14 calendar days to remediate; if Redwood cannot restore the baseline within that period, Customer may request a rollback of the added capacity and a pro-rata credit for the period in which the degraded performance persisted."

Notes and asks for Cirrus legal:
- Confirm whether 15% is acceptable as a threshold; if not, suggest an alternative metric or point us to the baseline in your monitoring dashboard.
- We recommend retaining the Exhibit F cross-reference rather than embedding runbook text in the Change Order; it reduces amendment churn.
- On data retention: recommended language to add to section 4.1 confirming 12-month audit log retention and that logs will be accessible via secure request within 5 business days.
- We will provide SOC 2 Type II artifacts via our secure evidence room link (see link below) and note the production environment hosting for the new capacity will remain in the same customer-dedicated tenant unless the customer requests a separate private cluster (that would require a separate procurement path).

Attachment: CO_Cirrus_legal_markups.docx
Evidence link: https://secure.redwood.com/evidence/CirrusHealth/SOC2/2026

Karthik — pinging you for trading on price sensitivity: if Cirrus pushes back on the blended rate we drafted, do we have margin room to concede on month 1 credits or a shorter minimum term?

Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.com

2) If approved, I will initiate the DocuSign envelope and target a signature campaign the same day.
3) Billing start: effective on signature with a retroactive credit window of up to 30 days if production cutover predates the signature date — per the change order table.

Links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/4539 | DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/sign/ABC-DEF-1234

Thanks — I'll standby for confirmation and will prepare the envelope once we have sign-off.
